title: Appeal of 100 Victoria Street encampment ruling
subtitle: Delegates urged a safe tenting protocol and opposed the notwithstanding clause; council also confirmed by-laws and adjourned.
overview: At a special meeting, Regional Council voted to appeal the Ontario Superior Court's May 21, 2026 decision on the 100 Victoria Street encampment to the Ontario Court of Appeal {{vote:m1}}. The Chief Administrative Officer, working with the Regional Solicitor, was directed to take the steps needed to carry out the appeal.

The meeting began with about 30 delegations, most of them residents and advocates. Many asked council not to appeal and to develop a safe tenting protocol. The court's decision allows the Region to proceed with the Kitchener Central Transit Hub if there is an alternative place of last resort for encampment residents. Many delegates also opposed any provincial use of the notwithstanding clause.

The appeal means the legal dispute continues. Whether the Region will adopt a safe tenting protocol or identify an alternative site was not decided at this meeting. Council later confirmed the day's proceedings by by-law and adjourned.

decisions.detail: Council voted to appeal the May 21, 2026 Ontario Superior Court decision on the 100 Victoria Street encampment to the Ontario Court of Appeal {{vote:m1}}, and authorized the CAO, in consultation with the Regional Solicitor, to take all necessary steps.

debate: Many delegates urged council not to appeal and to develop a safe tenting protocol, citing the court's finding that the Region may proceed with the transit hub if an alternative place of last resort exists. They pointed to approaches in London and Thunder Bay.

Delegates said there are far fewer shelter beds than people experiencing homelessness, and that displacement leads to loss of belongings and contact with services. Some described tenting as a harm-reduction measure rather than adequate housing.
Many delegates opposed any provincial use of the notwithstanding clause. Some criticized the short-notice meeting time and the closed-session discussion beforehand.

One councillor spoke against the appeal, citing legal costs, uncertain chances of success and Charter concerns. Another supported it for legal clarity on municipal responsibilities, while saying more housing and policy work is needed.

Several councillors said homelessness needs coordinated action from provincial and federal governments and area municipalities, given the two-tier structure. One noted that an earlier motion to explore safe tenting had been defeated.
